svg.title: The graph interval construction used to pass from connected graphs to these trees is explicit. Fix an injective numerical ordering of the occurrence vertices and a root (0). For a connected graph H, let (d(v)) be shortest-path distance from (0). For every v ̸= 0, choose as parent the least ordered neighbor at distance (d(v)-1). The resulting parent edges form a ranked spanning tree. Its depth function is uniquely determined by its parent map: it is zero at the root and increases by one at every child. More generally any graph with this breadth-first parent has that same depth function, since every edge changes depth by at most one and the tree realizes the assigned depths. For a fixed tree p arising in this way, let Up be the subset of original graph edges satisfying both of the following requirements. Their endpoint depths differ by at most one.
